prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot to Shore Control Room), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory when capability<dispatch target; applies accepted ceiling). Public grid, port out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; blocks protection conflicts; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image, approved turbine state). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms to Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace). Substation Operator: switching, clearances; Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint modes. Grid Dispatcher: targets. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt to Cybersecurity Gateway; provides operating data for blade review), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss; records survey restrictions), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale; proposes survey dates), Work Permit Portal, Personnel Tracking Console. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy (forecasts/measurements), Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record). Modes: Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum, Crew Count Correction. Marine Coordinator, Field Supervisor: personnel accountability, escalations; Field Supervisor checks cyber requirements in briefings, uses Deferred Task Rationale for postponed cyber work. Records: time, location, role, disposition. Cyber: Cybersecurity Gateway monitors traffic; Cybersecurity Analyst produces Firmware Hash Attestation, preserves evidence, escalates. Incident lead classifies reports, assigns owner; isolate only affected connection without unsafe condition; Control Engineer, Electrical Technician coordinate changes with duty role; recovery only after containment confirmed; SCADA Engineer validates restoration; post-incident review. Blade inspection: Duty Planner confirms priority, coordinates access; Blade Specialist classifies damage from tile image; images linked to turbine, blade, date, angle, conditions; uncertain/growing/safety findings referred to close-access inspection.

New part:
S450: Close-access work is planned only after the responsible team verifies turbine isolation, rotor restraint, access arrangements, and rescue provisions.
S451: The HSE Officer reviews the work method, exposure controls, and emergency arrangements before personnel approach the rotor.
S452: The Blade Specialist examines the affected surface using suitable lighting, measurement tools, and nondestructive inspection methods.
S453: Defect records describe location, dimensions, orientation, suspected cause, confidence, and any change from earlier observations.
S454: Cracks, erosion, coating loss, lightning damage, bond-line indications, and drainage concerns are assessed against approved engineering criteria.
S455: The Blade Specialist distinguishes cosmetic damage from conditions that could affect structural integrity or safe turbine operation.
S456: When evidence is incomplete, the inspection record identifies the uncertainty and specifies additional measurements or imagery needed.
S457: The Field Supervisor confirms that close-access findings are documented before personnel leave the work area.
S458: The Maintenance Planning Engine uses the assessed severity, defect growth rate, weather exposure, and production impact to support repair prioritization.
S459: The Duty Planner assigns a target repair window and coordinates required personnel, equipment, and vessel capacity.
S460: The Storekeeper checks repair materials and tooling against the approved repair method before mobilization.
S461: The Service Operations Vessel prepares the Recovery Basket Load Sheet for the planned work activity.
S462: Repair plans identify surface preparation, material application, cure requirements, inspection hold points, and acceptance criteria.
S463: After repair, the Blade Specialist records the completed work and verifies that the repaired area meets the applicable acceptance criteria.
S464: The Duty Planner updates the maintenance record and schedules follow-up inspection when residual uncertainty or defect history warrants it.
S465: Port and berth coordination aligns vessel access with the readiness of offshore work, people, equipment, and permits.
S466: The Marine Coordinator maintains a rolling view of berth occupancy, planned arrivals, departure estimates, and vessel service requirements.
S467: Berth capacity is assessed against usable quay length, water depth, access routes, lifting arrangements, and local safety clearances.
S468: The port schedule includes time for arrival checks, passenger movements, cargo handling, refueling, and routine vessel servicing.
S469: The Duty Planner compares task readiness with the expected departure window before committing crews and equipment to a marine campaign.
S470: The Maintenance Planning Engine supports this review by presenting task duration, resource demand, and dependency status.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
